title: The day five cards halved
headline: Five cards halved in one reading on Nov 6. The list still shows it.
dek: On Nov 6, TCGplayer's market price for five cards fell 45% to 53% from the reading before: four 30th Celebration promos (Pikachu ex 107 and 109, Umbreon ex 110, Espeon ex 108) and one Delta Reign card (Eevee 114/103). By their Nov 9 readings all five are up from those Nov 6 lows, by 10% to 42%, while the 7-day list still reads four of them down 40% to 60%. Neither reading is wrong: they answer different questions. No sale was checked behind any of it.
why_now: Tuesday's File called Pikachu ex 107's move "a bounce, or a day." Two readings later all five are up from Nov 6, and the 7-day list keeps reading them down. That gap is worth explaining while it is open, because a list that compares this week with last week will say "down" for days after a price has turned.
risk: Five cards in two sets losing about half their market price on the same reading is a pattern in TCGplayer's price, not a fact we can explain from price data: the cause isn't visible here and no sale was checked behind any of it. The rebound is also thin: Pikachu ex 107 slipped from $47.78 to $46.49 on its latest reading, and Umbreon ex 110 and Espeon ex 108 have no reading on some days. The prices are TCGplayer's market price on the dates shown, not a daily series. The board's since-yesterday list never showed the Nov 6 drop: with no checked sale, a one-day move over 40% is left out by rule. The 7-day list showed it from Nov 7. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether the cards leave the 7-day list around Nov 13 and Nov 14. By the list's rule the week it compares against has to stop containing the pre-Nov 6 readings first, so a card leaving then is the list catching up, not a new move. Whether any of the five goes back to its Nov 6 low ($35 for the Pikachu promos, $79 for Umbreon ex 110, $59 for Espeon ex 108, $21 for Eevee). And the label: Mission Control is starting to store checked eBay sales for a short list of tracked cards; the morning one of these cards has one, its row stops reading Unconfirmed.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, from the board's published lists of Nov 3 to Nov 10, 2026 (prices Nov 2 to Nov 9); the Nov 10 list for the table

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The drop: each card's market price on the board's list one reading before Nov 6 against its Nov 6 reading (Pikachu ex 107 $68.40 to $35.30, Pikachu ex 109 $66.23 to $35.28, Umbreon ex 110 $142.75 to $79.13, Espeon ex 108 $125.66 to $58.92, Eevee 114/103 $37.39 to $20.60). The rise: each card's Nov 9 reading against its Nov 6 reading ($46.49, $38.67, $90.67, $77.35, $29.32). The table: the four of the five on the board's Nov 10 list (Pikachu ex 109 has left it), prices Nov 2 to Nov 9, the change between 3-day medians at each end; start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, then rounded to the dollar, so within a dollar. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades. The since-yesterday list: 3% or more, 40% or less without a checked sale. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
